cim: SDAIA launches initiative to spread artificial intelligence at Saudi universities
cim_eredeti: SDAIA launches initiative to spread artificial intelligence at Saudi universities
szoveg_eredeti:
Saudi Data and Artificial Intelligence Authority (SDAIA) has launched the «Year of Artificial Intelligence in Saudi Universities» initiative, part of its efforts to expand the use of smart technologies in educational and research institutions, develop national skills able to keep pace with rapid technological change, and turn academic knowledge and student ideas into innovative projects and solutions that support the kingdom's digital transformation.

The initiative includes a package of activities and programs spanning scientific seminars, discussion sessions, training workshops, interactive booths and specialized consultations. It targets university students, faculty members and administrative staff, aiming to broaden knowledge of AI technologies, promote their responsible use and improve how their applications are used in education, scientific research and administrative work.

The move is part of the kingdom's drive to build national human capabilities able to keep pace with advances in artificial intelligence and to strengthen the role of universities in producing knowledge and innovation, in line with the targets of Saudi Vision 2030 and its push toward an economy built on data and advanced technologies.

The «Year of Artificial Intelligence in Saudi Universities» initiative aims to strengthen the role of universities as incubators of knowledge, scientific research and innovation, and as a key partner in preparing national talent able to make use of modern technologies and develop their applications.

The initiative also works to widen the use of artificial intelligence within the educational environment by introducing students, faculty members and administrative staff to the capabilities and limits of these technologies, and explaining their impact on the nature of jobs and the skills required in the coming years.

Through these programs, SDAIA seeks to link theoretical knowledge with practical application, so that participants can apply smart tools in their fields of specialization, use them to improve the quality of academic and administrative work, and develop research and innovation projects.

The initiative also focuses on raising awareness of responsible practices in the use of artificial intelligence, particularly data protection, verifying the reliability of outputs and understanding the limits of smart systems, ensuring these technologies are deployed safely and effectively within educational institutions.

The initiative rests on three main tracks that progress from spreading awareness of modern technologies to training and hands-on application, and finally to measuring results and documenting outcomes.

The first track builds awareness of artificial intelligence concepts and responsible uses, offering content that explains the nature of these technologies, their capabilities and limits, along with their impact on various sectors and the future of jobs and the labor market.

The second track focuses on moving to practical application through specialized training programs designed to enable university audiences to use artificial intelligence tools in their work and studies, and to develop the skills needed to handle smart applications and use them to carry out various tasks.

The third track measures the initiative's impact, documents its outputs and tracks the development opportunities it generates, helping to evaluate the results of training programs and to identify ideas and projects that can be developed and turned into sustainable applications within universities.

The approach aims to link educational and training activities to results that can be tracked and evaluated, while strengthening opportunities to turn acquired knowledge into practical applications that raise the quality of education and scientific research and the efficiency of administrative work.

The initiative includes organizing scientific seminars and panel discussions on the rapid advances in artificial intelligence technologies, their impact on the labor market, the future of jobs, and the skills various sectors will need in the coming phase.

These sessions examine the capabilities of intelligent systems and the limits on their use, and review their applications across academic and professional disciplines and their role in raising productivity, improving performance and speeding up the completion of work.

The events also address the principles of responsible use of AI, including the protection of personal and institutional data, verifying the accuracy of information produced by intelligent systems, and handling outputs with awareness so that they can be put to use without unexamined reliance on them.

These sessions allow students and faculty members to learn about the shifts AI technologies are bringing to the nature of professions and job tasks, and to review the new skills the labor market requires as institutions expand their use of smart tools.

The initiative includes applied training workshops aimed at three main groups within universities — faculty members, students and administrative staff — with programs tailored to the nature of each group's tasks and professional needs.

Programs for faculty members enable them to put AI to work in teaching and scientific research and to draw on its applications to develop teaching methods, prepare academic content and improve the efficiency of research activities.

Programs for students focus on developing their technical skills and helping them turn their ideas into projects and early-stage solutions that can be built on, strengthening their capacity to innovate and to develop products and applications that respond to the needs of society and economic sectors.

For administrative staff, the workshops aim to raise institutional performance by introducing smart applications that can be used to improve the quality of work and speed up day-to-day transactions and tasks, and by developing ways of managing information and operations within university institutions.

The programs seek to prepare a university environment better equipped to handle technological change by enabling the various groups to use AI in line with their practical needs and strengthening their ability to benefit from the opportunities these technologies offer.

The initiative features a set of interactive booths that let participants learn about SDAIA's services and products, submit proposals and ideas, and obtain specialized consultations that help them develop their projects.

The «SDAIA Publications» booth introduces the knowledge products and publications the authority offers in data and AI, giving students and faculty members knowledge resources that help them keep up with developments in these fields.

The program also includes the «Tawakkalna welcomes your ideas» booth, which receives students« proposals for developing the comprehensive national app Tawakkalna and opens the way for them to contribute ideas that help improve digital services and enhance the user experience.

The «Session with Your Advisor» zone offers participants specialist consultations, helping them shape their student ideas and projects, identify the right paths to develop them and turn them into workable solutions.

The «Your Gateway to Data» zone reviews the Kingdom's laws and regulations on data and artificial intelligence, aiming to raise awareness of the regulatory frameworks governing how data is handled and smart technologies are used.

The program also includes a «Capacity Building» zone, linked to efforts to empower participants and sharpen their technical skills, supporting the initiative's goals of spreading knowledge and widening access to training programs.

The initiative gives university students and faculty members the chance to secure training places and join programs offered through the «Athka X» capacity-building platform, one of the tools used to support training and the development of national skills.
